text:
Brandon Duhaime joined Toronto as a fourth-line energy forward, and his month has been more about Arber Xhekaj than the scoresheet. After Xhekaj criticized a gloveless punch, TSN's headline had Duhaime saying "Let him talk." He has 63 hits in 24 games, which is the job.

The offense is thin even for that job: 4 points, one goal, and nothing in his last ten games. His shooting is at 5%, under half the league norm, so a goal or two would be normal. But the Leafs get only 42% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there, five points worse than without him, and they've lost nine of the last ten he's played.

The case for him lives in last season's numbers. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting fewer expected chances with him on the ice, 98th percentile among forwards, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 61% of his zone exits leaving with possession. That defense hasn't shown up in Toronto yet. On about 12 minutes a night, watch whether Jim Hiller keeps him in the lineup or shortens the bench.
headline: Duhaime brings the edge, not the offense
